agent_notes: Timing is inferred: the mountains must be covered before the waters peak, and 7:24 says the waters prevailed 150 days. Offset 40 days from the start with a 20-day margin is an estimate. The 15 cubits of 7:20 is not a duration and is not dated.

7:5 is a summary of Noah's obedience; I read it as the seven-day preparation (Radak: stocking and arranging the ark while it stood open), and give it the full week so the entry falls exactly on the day of 7:11/7:13. Radak holds that Noah went in at the START of the seven days; the plain order of 7:10 and 7:13 puts the entry on the last day, which I follow.

Rashi: the first day is not counted in the forty (the night belongs to the previous Hebrew day), so the forty days end on 28 Kislev (R. Eliezer). I count forty days from the start of the rain, giving the same end within a day.

The verbs in 7:11 are passive, so God is not listed as agent in this event; the waters are. The judgment instance names the LORD as initiator because the story (6:13, 7:4) presents the flood as His act.

agent_notes: Reviewer requests applied. (1) The divine-name shift is stated within the verse: Elohim commands, YHWH shuts the door; the chapter alternates (YHWH in 7:1 and 7:5, Elohim in 7:9 and 7:16a). I do not build a source-critical theory on it. (2) The 'blunt anatomical term' sentence is dropped; זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה is the ordinary pair, also used of humans in Gen 1:27. The note on נְקֵבָה keeps only the root. (3) 'Sevens of clean animals' is used, not 'pairs'.

בְּעַד: Rashi reads 'against / in front of' (shut it off from the water); Radak reads 'protected'; Ibn Ezra reads a closing that was a mercy. The literal layer says 'behind him', the plain sense of בַּעַד; the dramatic layer lets the closing sound final and protective without adding a fact.

notes.note: Calendar: the Flood's day is quoted in the text's own calendar (7:11, 'second month, seventeenth day'). anchor.flood is Noah's 600th year taken as day 1 of that year, so the second month, 17th day is 1 month (29.53 d) + 16 d = 45.53 days. Whether the year starts at Tishri (R. Eliezer: Marcheshvan; Targum Pseudo-Jonathan) or Nisan (R. Joshua: Iyar) changes the season, not the offset from the year start; the 1-month margin on the command covers the uncertainty of the year start. The linker's civil date label for this day is nominal.

Verse 7:6 (Noah's age, 'the flood was upon the earth') is included in evt.gen_7.noah_enters_ark as the age date of the entry. Every verse of the chapter is covered. Gen 8 will likely fulfil 7:24 and the 150 days; the link is for that chapter's session. Gen 6:18-21 commands about entry and animals are linked to the entry here.
